lead.tldr: SpaceX IPO bringing 18,712 BTC onto Nasdaq-100 may trigger passive rebalancing out of other tech, pressuring Bitcoin • IREN’s full‑stack AI infrastructure strategy secures $3.4bn NVIDIA contract, signaling demand for vertically integrated compute assets • EU’s €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund under EQT will intensify capital competition for European deep‑tech founders • Minnesota’s new crypto‑custody law empowers local banks, potentially diverting deposit flows from national crypto platforms • OKX‑ICE oil perpetual futures give 120 million retail users regulated exposure, accelerating crypto‑traditional finance convergence • THORChain exploit highlights ongoing vulnerability of cross‑chain protocols, recovery plan must avoid token dilution

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO will place 18,712 BTC on the Nasdaq‑100, highlighting fresh Bitcoin exposure for mega‑caps. Meanwhile, AI‑infrastructure deals from IREN and WhiteFiber fuel a hardware surge and Europe’s €5 billion Scaleup Fund readies to back crypto‑enabled scale‑ups.

top_signals.title: Space X IPO Is
top_signals.summary: SpaceX is preparing a $75 billion initial public offering that could quickly join the Nasdaq‑100. Inclusion would bring the company’s 18,712 BTC holdings onto the index, increasing Bitcoin exposure among mega‑cap stocks. Analysts warn that passive fund rebalancing required by the fast‑entry rule may pull capital from other technology names, creating downside pressure for Bitcoin.

top_signals.title: AI infrastructure race heats up as IREN pitches full-stack strategy, WhiteFiber lands $160M deal
top_signals.summary: IREN co‑founder Dan Roberts says the primary constraint on AI growth is physical infrastructure and the firm is pursuing a vertically integrated model that includes power generation, data centers, GPUs and software. IREN has secured a five‑year AI cloud contract with NVIDIA valued at $3.4 billion and it currently operates roughly 5 GW of grid‑connected capacity. WhiteFiber signed a five‑year AI compute agreement with a French technology customer for more than $160 million. The deals highlight accelerating demand for end‑to‑end AI infrastructure in North America and Europe and suggest potential revenue streams for investors focused on the hardware and services layers of the AI stack.

top_signals.title: 100+ companies the €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund could back
top_signals.summary: The European Union has appointed Swedish investment firm EQT to manage the newly created €5 billion Scaleup Europe Fund, the continent’s largest tech‑focused fund. The fund is structured to back more than 100 high‑growth European scale‑ups, providing capital to accelerate their expansion. This appointment ends a closely watched competition among leading European investors and underscores a coordinated effort to strengthen Europe’s technology ecosystem.

top_signals.title: Why Minnesota is empowering local banks to fight Wall Street for crypto revenue
top_signals.summary: Minnesota has enacted a pioneering law that authorizes state‑chartered banks and credit unions to provide cryptocurrency custody services. The legislation is designed to stem the outflow of deposits to out‑of‑state crypto platforms. By allowing local institutions to offer digital‑asset custody, the state aims to keep them competitive with Wall Street firms that are expanding into digital‑asset infrastructure. The measure will take effect in August 2026 and signals a regulatory approach that could attract institutional crypto activity to regional banks.

top_signals.title: Wall Street and crypto are merging again as OKX rolls out traditional oil benchmarks
top_signals.summary: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and the cryptocurrency exchange OKX have announced a partnership to issue perpetual oil futures linked to ICE’s Brent and WTI benchmarks. The products will be made available on OKX’s platform, which serves roughly 120 million retail users. By tying the contracts to established energy benchmarks, the collaboration brings regulated commodity exposure into the crypto ecosystem. Regulators have indicated that they will oversee these perpetual derivatives, underscoring the increasing convergence of traditional finance and digital asset markets.

top_signals.title: New Federal Reserve Chair Sworn In, but Rate Cut Odds Remain at 0
top_signals.summary: Kevin Warsh has been sworn in as the new Federal Reserve Chair, signaling continuity in the Fed’s leadership. CME FedWatch data indicates that the probability of an interest‑rate cut in 2026 is effectively zero and market participants are pricing in additional hikes later in the year. This sustained tight monetary policy is expected to pressure risk‑on assets, including Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, which could affect institutional exposure to digital assets.

top_signals.title: THORChain
top_signals.summary: THORChain, a cross‑chain liquidity protocol, experienced a $10.7 million exploit when a malicious node reconstructed a vault private key using a GG20 threshold‑signature vulnerability. In response, the network halted all trading activity and deployed a software patch to close the identified flaw. The team is now evaluating a recovery strategy that does not involve minting or selling additional RUNE tokens, aiming to protect existing token holders and maintain market confidence.

top_signals.title: Trump Media moved but 'did not sell' $205 million in bitcoin amid rising losses on crypto bets
top_signals.summary: Trump Media & Technology Group transferred 2,650 Bitcoin, valued at roughly $205 million, to the Crypto.com platform. The company emphasized that the assets were moved and not sold, leaving a $455 million unrealized loss on its Bitcoin holdings. The transfer comes after Trump Media withdrew its application for a spot Bitcoin exchange‑traded fund. The move follows a reported $405.9 million net loss for the first quarter, underscoring the firm’s exposure to cryptocurrency market volatility.

top_signals.title: Tokenized Stocks: What Traditional Exchanges Stand to Lose
top_signals.summary: Institutional investors should note that the SEC's proposed innovation exemption would allow third parties to create tokenized representations of listed equities without the underlying company's consent. This could divert trading volume and fee income from established stock exchanges to decentralized platforms. The shift may alter the infrastructure for equity settlement and raise regulatory and custody considerations for large investors.
